attempts.raw_response: According to local reports, the men were accused of facilitating the women's attendance at the wedding, which was deemed a violation of tribal customs. The video sparked outrage among conservative elders, who allegedly ordered the killings. The women themselves were also targeted; Bazeegha and Sereen Jan were shot dead, while Begum Jan and Amina survived the attack. Shaheen, the minor, was reportedly killed alongside them. The acquittals have sparked protests from human rights groups, who argue that the court failed to deliver justice. The case highlights the ongoing struggle between traditional tribal codes and modern legal standards in Pakistan's remote regions.

pair.human_continuation: It also showed a man dancing - although they were never in the same shot together. A second man is said to have been filming. It was enough, in the remote northern Kohistan district where matters of family honour are settled in blood, to warrant at least three of the women's deaths. According to local custom, male family members of a woman suspected of an out-of-wedlock liaison - even of a seemingly innocuous nature - should first kill the woman, and then go after the man. The family of the man would not oppose this action, correspondents say. It meant everyone in the video - which was seen as "breaching the honour" of the women's family - was in danger. How did it come to light?
pair.prefix: Five other men were acquitted by the court in Besham, in north-western Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Why were they killed? The exact details of what took place are not entirely clear. A video emerged in 2011 which appeared to show a group of women - named as Bazeegha, Sereen Jan, Begum Jan and Amina - at a wedding, singing and clapping. A fifth woman - Shaheen, who was under 18 - is also thought to have been present.

source_document.title: Kohistan video murders: Three guilty in 'honour killing' blood feud
